title: Istanbul to Mardin, Şanlıurfa & Gaziantep: Direct Flight Strategy

metaDescription: Plan direct flights from IST and SAW to Gaziantep (GZT), Şanlıurfa (GNY), and Mardin (MQM) with open-jaw routing, transfers, and winter fog tips.
quickAnswer: Direct flights from Istanbul (IST and SAW) reach Gaziantep (GZT) in 1 hour 40 minutes, Şanlıurfa GAP (GNY) in 1 hour 50 minutes, and Mardin (MQM) in 2 hours. Gaziantep has the highest daily frequency, making an open-jaw route—flying into GZT and out of MQM—the cleanest way to cover Upper Mesopotamia without backtracking.

body.text: Which airport (GZT, GNY, MQM) has the most reliable daily flights from IST and SAW?

[Gaziantep Airport (GZT)](https://dhmi.gov.tr/Sayfalar/Havalimani/Gaziantep/AnaSayfa.aspx) offers the highest daily frequency and strongest recovery options if a flight is delayed, with multiple daily nonstops operated by Turkish Airlines from Istanbul Airport (IST) and by [Pegasus Airlines](https://www.flypgs.com/en) and [AJet](https://ajet.com/en-tr/flights-from-istanbul-to-gaziantep) from Sabiha Gökçen (SAW). [Şanlıurfa GAP Airport (GNY)](https://dhmi.gov.tr/Sayfalar/Havalimani/Gap/AnaSayfa.aspx) and [Mardin Prof. Dr. Aziz Sancar Airport (MQM)](https://dhmi.gov.tr/Sayfalar/Havalimani/Mardin/AnaSayfa.aspx) also enjoy year-round direct flights from both IST and SAW, but run fewer daily frequencies.
Live domestic departures and arrivals for all three terminals are published on the [DHMİ flight information portal](https://dhmi.gov.tr/Sayfalar/TumUcuslar.aspx).
How do you plan an open-jaw Mesopotamia trip (fly into Gaziantep, out of Mardin)?

Booking two one-way domestic flights—landing in Gaziantep (GZT) and departing from Mardin (MQM)—saves a full 4.5-to-5-hour return drive across the southeastern plateau. Domestic Turkish airlines price one-way tickets at roughly half of a round-trip fare, so open-jaw routing costs virtually nothing extra while letting you move steadily east from Gaziantep to Şanlıurfa and on to Mardin.
A well-paced 5-to-7-day west-to-east progression works cleanly:

items: Days 1–2 (Gaziantep): Fly into GZT, explore the Zeugma Mosaic Museum, historic copper bazaar, and baklava workshops.

Days 3–4 (Halfeti & Şanlıurfa): Drive east (about 2 hours direct, or 3.5 hours via a Euphrates boat stop in Halfeti) to visit Göbeklitepe, Karahantepe, Balıklıgöl, and the Şanlıurfa Archaeology Museum.

Days 5–6 (Mardin, Dara & Midyat): Continue east along the broad D400 highway (about 2 hours 30 minutes from Şanlıurfa to Old Mardin) to explore stone mansions, Deyrulzafaran Monastery, Dara Ancient City, and Midyat before flying home from MQM.

body.text: If you rent a car in Gaziantep and drop it at Mardin Airport, confirm the one-way drop fee upfront with major national agencies; for groups of two to four, hiring a dedicated regional driver-vehicle often compares favorably once one-way rental surcharges and Old Mardin parking friction are included.
How far are the airports from old-town boutique hotels?

Gaziantep Airport (GZT) sits about 20 km southeast of the historic Bey District and castle quarter (25 to 35 minutes by taxi or private transfer). Mardin Prof. Dr. Aziz Sancar Airport (MQM) lies on the plain near Kızıltepe, roughly 20 km below the hilltop old town—a 25-to-35-minute climb up the switchbacks. Şanlıurfa GAP Airport (GNY) is the farthest out at 35 to 40 km north of Balıklıgöl (40 to 50 minutes).

Old Mardin requires special last-mile planning. Its narrow pedestrian stone lanes and stepped alleys mean transfer vehicles often drop guests along Birinci Cadde (First Street), where hotel porters meet you to carry suitcases down stone stairs. Confirm your exact drop-off point with your boutique hotel before landing.
What seasonal fog delays happen in winter?

Between late November and February, radiation fog frequently settles across the flat Mesopotamian plain around Şanlıurfa GAP (GNY) and Mardin (MQM), especially between 05:30 and 10:30 AM. Dense low-visibility fog can delay morning departures or divert incoming flights to Diyarbakır (DIY) or Gaziantep (GZT) until midday sun clears the runway.
Protect your international return from Istanbul with this winter flight checklist:

items: Favor midday flights in winter: Schedule departures out of MQM or GNY between 11:30 and 16:00 rather than first-wave 07:00 flights whenever possible.
Never book a tight same-day international connection: Leave at least 5 to 6 hours—or an overnight stay in Istanbul—between a winter southeastern domestic flight and a long-haul departure from IST.

Keep a single-ticket itinerary for tight links: If you must connect same day at IST, book both legs on a single Turkish Airlines ticket so the carrier rebooks you automatically if fog delays MQM or GNY.
Check airport codes carefully: Confirm whether your Istanbul flight uses IST (European side) or SAW (Asian side) before booking onward transfers or hotels.

faq.q: Are there direct flights from Istanbul Airport (IST) to Mardin (MQM)?
faq.a: Yes. Turkish Airlines operates direct year-round flights from Istanbul Airport (IST) to Mardin Prof. Dr. Aziz Sancar Airport (MQM), while Pegasus Airlines and AJet operate direct flights from Sabiha Gökçen Airport (SAW).

faq.q: Which direction is better: Gaziantep to Mardin or Mardin to Gaziantep?
faq.a: Both directions work equally well. Starting in Gaziantep (GZT) and finishing in Mardin (MQM) builds gradually from culinary heritage to ancient Göbeklitepe and hilltop stone architecture, while reversing the order puts your final departure at higher-frequency GZT.

faq.q: How long is the drive from Gaziantep to Şanlıurfa and then to Mardin?
faq.a: Gaziantep to Şanlıurfa takes roughly 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours on the O-52 motorway (longer if detouring to Halfeti). Şanlıurfa to Mardin takes about 2 hours 30 minutes along the D400 highway.

faq.q: Are Havaş airport buses available at GZT, GNY, and MQM?
faq.a: Yes. Scheduled airport shuttle buses (Havaş or municipal shuttles) meet arriving flights at Gaziantep, Şanlıurfa GAP, and Mardin airports, though private transfers are far easier if your boutique hotel sits deep inside Old Mardin or historic Gaziantep.

faq.q: Can you fly directly from Antalya or Izmir to Gaziantep or Mardin?
faq.a: Yes, direct seasonal and year-round flights connect Izmir (ADB) and Antalya (AYT) to Gaziantep (GZT) and Mardin (MQM) several days a week, mainly via SunExpress and Pegasus, though daily frequencies are lower than from Istanbul.

faq.q: What is the best month to fly into Southeast Türkiye for clear weather?
faq.a: April, May, October, and early November offer the clearest skies, mild daytime temperatures (18–26°C), and minimal winter fog risk, avoiding both July–August 40°C heatwaves and December–January runway fog.
